evals.name: readme-quickstart-for-ledger
evals.prompt: New people on the team keep asking me how to run ledger locally and the only doc we have is docs/setup-old.md, which is from 2023 and wrong. Please write a README.md for this repo so a developer on their first day can run it and see one summary without asking anyone. It is plain Python 3, nothing to install; the suite is `python -m unittest discover -s tests`. Deal with the old doc however makes sense.
evals.expected_output: Reader line written (first-day developer, "how do I run ledger locally"), type README quickstart, docs/setup-old.md found by the grep and retired. README.md laid out with Quickstart, Configuration, Develop and Where-things-are headings; the run command `python -m ledger summarise sample.csv` pasted with its real output line `3 entries, total 120.50 EUR` after running it in the session; a configuration table with the three keys the code reads (LEDGER_DATA_DIR, LEDGER_CURRENCY, LEDGER_API_KEY) and LEDGER_API_KEY marked required, with the export above the run command; the unittest command with its `Ran 2 tests` line; no TODO, TBD, latest or simply; docs/setup-old.md deleted or reduced to a pointer in the same change; first 30 lines show install, run and expected output.

checks.text: The repo was searched for an existing doc on the topic before writing
The run command was executed in the session, not typed from memory
The command ran before the README that quotes it was written
The test command was executed so its count line could be pasted
README has the Quickstart heading of the template
README carries the exact run command
README carries the real output line of the run command
Both optional keys the code reads are documented
The test command's count line is quoted
No placeholder or filler word survived the phase 3 grep
No Introduction section restating the name
The stale doc is gone or no longer carries the wrong instruction (deleted or reduced to a pointer)
Only the README and the old doc changed; no source or test edits
The reply does not invent an install step for a stdlib-only project

expectations: Phase 1 done: the transcript or reply states the reader line in the shape `Reader: <role>, arrives with "<question>", leaves able to <action>` (a first-day developer who wants to run ledger locally), names the type as README quickstart, and records the grep result as `edit README.md` with docs/setup-old.md identified as the existing hit to retire.
Phase 2 done: README.md holds the template headings (Quickstart, Configuration, Develop, Where things are) in that order; no heading was renamed or dropped without a stated reason.

Phase 3 done: every fenced command in README.md (`python -m ledger summarise sample.csv`, `python -m unittest discover -s tests`) was run in the session and is followed by its first real output line (`3 entries, total 120.50 EUR`, `Ran 2 tests`); the configuration table lists exactly the three keys the code reads, obtained by grepping for os.environ rather than recalled, with LEDGER_API_KEY marked required and the export placed above the run command; the grep for TODO, TBD, latest, simply and just run prints nothing.

Phase 4 done: the quickstart was re-run from a clean location (a fresh clone, copy or container, or at minimum a fresh shell with no LEDGER_API_KEY set so the missing-key failure is seen and the export added), and `head -30 README.md` shows the run command and its expected output; where lychee or markdownlint are unavailable the reply says so instead of claiming they passed.

Phase 5 done: docs/setup-old.md is deleted or reduced to a single pointer to README.md in the same change, the README is the only file matching a grep for the topic, and the reply's claim that the docs are updated is stated against the diff rather than assumed.
